To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
monitoring is a means of power that shapes a social reality and contributes to give the park a material dimension, but it does not necessarily guide action and management.

monitoring programmes are not only a simple tool to guide nature conservation actions but are also a means to provide national parks with an effective and legitimate existence in the eyes of the public.
monitoring programmes in tropical national parks are not only technical instruments but also contribute to shape the social reality of the parks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social construction of monitoring and the way it contributes to shape the social life of parks and their relations with their surrounding communities.
the role of science and technique in the construction of a postcolonial nature conservation.
the question of how the production of knowledge and its implementation in the field can shape the social reality of conservation and the distribution of power.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the monitoring programmes are not only a means to provide the parks with scientific knowledge and to guide their management but also to give them an existence and an identity.
the monitoring programmes we analysed are not only technical tools but also political tools.
monitoring is not a simple technical choice and should be considered as an important social process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
monitoring programmes are a means for parks to exist, and not necessarily to be effective.
the monitoring programmes are not a simple technical choice, but a political and cognitive choice.
monitoring is a social practice that is embedded in the social and political contexts of the park.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the implementation of monitoring is a complex social process, involving a wide range of social and political dimensions that should be better taken into account by the international conservation community.
the use of indicators and monitoring instruments is a political choice that has a direct effect on the social organisation of nature conservation and on the power relationships in national parks.

the implementation of a monitoring programme is an opportunity to reflect upon and to discuss the cognitive and social representation of nature and conservation in the parks and to reorientate the conservation action accordingly.
